frontier.hypothesis: F32 — tools/ra_solver/inverse.py local can type the block-3 seat residual REACHABLE or FORECLOSED and name the C-lever vectors, converting this function's disposition from an exhaustion argument into a proof.
frontier.mechanism: The classify verdict names inverse.py as the next tool, and this session extracted the QTYDBG attribution (block 3 quantities, births, deaths, refs, allocation order and the reproduced qty_compare priorities) that the 2026-08-30 campaign said was missing. find_free_reg's ascending scan gives a closed-form condition for target's $a0 seat: both $v0 and $v1 occupied across the chain's whole span at allocation time.
frontier.next_probe: Run inverse.py local against CD_datasync block 3 with a HAND-VERIFIED --goal-order (perturb.py --goal-from-target currently SKIPS this block: 'goal is not a topological order, 2 violations', because difflib mis-pairs the duplicate sll / lw skeletons — fix needs anchor-based alignment, which is an operator-lane change to tools/). frontier.hypothesis: The standing family trigger: a JOINT sched.c-emission-order x global.c/local-alloc.c-seat solver closes CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready together.
frontier.mechanism: Every C change that fixes the emission order breaks the register seats and vice versa — proven over 20 sessions here, 68 on CD_ready and 107 on CD_sync. The current solver suite is single-axis, which is why all three twins land on the same disposition. This session's classify result (RA first, with an ordering component behind it) is further evidence the two axes are coupled rather than separable.
frontier.next_probe: When a joint solver exists, re-open CD_datasync, CD_sync and CD_ready as ONE basin. Use the s19 dual-fork harness (tmp/grind/CD_datasync/s19/: psx.sh + score.py + expand.py + sweep.sh, ~1.5 s/form, ~15x cheaper than a sandbox run, function-agnostic apart from the hardcoded name) as the scoring loop.

frontier.hypothesis: C bodies for the five asm-only Intr consumers would make the Ruling D aggregate-merge scope grant spendable across the twin family.
frontier.mechanism: Prong (c) requires the merge to be COMPLETE — every merged per-word symbol removed from C AND from the splat symbol config. getintr, CD_cw, func_800817A0 (CD_flush), func_800819C4 and func_80081E1C reference D_800A1494/95/96 from assembly (48 sites total), and CD_cw additionally references D_800F19B8/BC/C0 (14 sites), so the per-word symbols cannot be retired while those bodies are INCLUDE_ASM.
frontier.next_probe: Completeness trigger only, and a LOW-value one on this evidence: this session measured the merge as byte-identical to the existing pointer-local spelling, so unblocking prong (c) would not move CD_datasync's residual. Record it so a future session does not re-derive the blocker; do not prioritise it as a closing lever.
